name: TFI International Inc.
moat_justification: Scale and a proven decentralized acquisition platform in a fragmented industry, but freight is a commodity with low switching costs: ROIC proxy fell from 24.4% in FY2022 to 8.6% in FY2025 and operating margin from 13.0% to 7.2% through the freight recession, showing no pricing power that survives the cycle.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
BUYBACK_TAILWIND: share count shrinking 3.0%/yr — already credited via the growth adjustment
BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT: a >60% revenue jump/drop in the last 5 yrs — check for divestitures, big M&A, or restatements before trusting any CAGR
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2024, 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base

ADS_RATIO_APPLIED: 40-F filer — per-share figures scaled x1.0 ordinary shares per ADS (Form 40-F for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-02-17), cover page: securities registered under Section 12(b) are 'Common Shares', trading symbol TFII, listed on the New York Stock Exchange; the cover states 84,408,437 common shares outstanding, matching the engine's dei count) so they are comparable to the ADS price; TTM pins are taken as per-ADS already
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 4.2x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
HIGH_NET_DEBT: net debt is 3.7x normalized OE — levered OE can vanish fast; stress the bear cases
TIER_BAND: bear-case tier D (7.5%) vs bull-case tier C (11.9%) — the verdict spans tiers; size any position to the bear end
one_liner: North American trucking consolidator, moat 4/10 — Tier C: weighted IRR 10.0%, IV@15% $66.54 vs $111.59 price; does not clear the 15% hurdle until ~$67, and with the bear case at 7.5% (Tier D) any position should be sized to the bear end.
moat_for: Scale: one of North America's largest trucking groups and the largest flatbed/specialized carrier via Daseke, with LTL terminal-network density from TForce Freight (ex-UPS Freight)
Decentralized acquisition platform under Alain Bedard: decades of buying fragmented carriers cheaply, keeping local brands/operators and improving their operating ratios
Diversification across LTL, Truckload and Logistics and across industrial end markets cushions any single freight lane
moat_against: Commodity freight, low shipper switching costs, deep rival set (Old Dominion, XPO, ArcBest, FedEx Freight, Heartland) — no network effect or lock-in
Returns have compressed through the cycle: ROIC proxy 24.4% (FY2022) to 8.6% (FY2025), operating margin 13.0% to 7.2% — pricing power does not hold in a freight recession
Cyclical and cost-exposed: unionized U.S. LTL workforce, driver and purchased-transportation cost pressure flagged into Q3 2026
Acquisition-led model carries leverage (net debt 3.7x normalized OE) and execution risk (Daseke integration/separation talk, planned U.S. redomiciliation)
